# Record 20260807-051433-7845f17

- **Record ID**: 20260807-051433-7845f17
- **Claim**: README.md#target-specification -- INL / DNL < 1 LSB (< 0.5 LSB stretch), untrimmed and uncalibrated, NOMINAL design over the PVT grid. The ratified row's binding condition names 3 sigma Monte Carlo mismatch, which sim/mc-cdac-mismatch/ owns; this record is the complementary environmental half of the same row (spec/monte-carlo-methodology-memo.md Sec 4). Also substantiates the note [d] claim that the endpoint-fit residual of the ratified switch and drive network is what lands in this row, the linear part having been moved to Gain error, systematic by DR-0012.
- **Netlist provenance**: extracted (star-split in-path, remediated) -- the --pdk gf180mcuD parasitic extraction of adc_top (layout/adc-top/parasitics/reports/20260806-230838-56be937/adc_top.para.spice, ~1300 devices, 2936 parasitic R + 156 parasitic C), taken with the klayout-tools 875eac3 pin PR #119 landed: klayout-tools#593 gives every device terminal on a net its own leg node with a distance-weighted series resistor back to the net hub, so two terminals on one net are now separated by real layout-dependent resistance. The superseded record 20260806-052258-8d36824 was taken on the PREVIOUS extraction, whose whole per-net resistance sat on a dead-end stub no device terminal was behind (layout/adc-top/parasitics/records/20260806-parasitic-topology.md), i.e. 156 R that carried no signal current. NOT full distributed per-segment RC -- klayout-tools#592 Option 2 remains out of scope upstream. Then locally remediated by layout/adc-top/parasitics/remediate_extracted.py: every anonymous PMOS-body (Nwell) net rewritten to vdd (local remediation of the klt PMOS-body gap; upstream 2AMLogic/klayout-tools#555 closed via #581, but that shipped only anonymous-net JSON surfacing, not an automatic re-tie-to-vdd, so this remediation is still necessary), the internal per-side input rails brought out as .SUBCKT pins, and the MiM caps left as their native PDK cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield subckt calls (no rewrite). NOT raw klt extract output. The extracted ADC_TOP core is wired into a schematic-level comparator + rung-1 SAR controller + DR-0013 input-drive network by layout/adc-top/parasitics/gen_extracted_inl_dnl_tb.py, which ports gen_adc_top.py's own input ladder and ideal shadow DAC verbatim so this run uses the UNMODIFIED sim/adc-inl-dnl/testbench/tb.json manifest (`sim/adc-inl-dnl/testbench/tb_adc_inl_dnl_extracted.spice`)
- **Corner matrix run**:
  - Process: tt, cap_ff, cap_ss, mim_ff, mim_ss, moscap_ff, moscap_ss
  - Temperature: -40 °C, 27 °C, 125 °C
  - Supply: 2.97 V, 3.30 V, 3.63 V
  - 63 point full-factorial grid (process × temperature × supply), 63 completed
  - Full PVT matrix per CLAUDE.md (−40/27/125 °C, ±10 % supply, process corners).
- **Statistical convention**: N/A (corner-matrix claim, not a distribution claim)
- **Linearity methodology**: `reduced-code-set-major-carry` — 18 probed transitions (1, 2, 128, 129, 255, 256, 257, 384, 511, 512, 513, 640, 767, 768, 769, 896, 1022, 1023) targeted at DR-0011's OWN array: the weight-256 sub-array MSB carry at 255->256 and 767->768 (the largest charge-division ratio this array forms, and independently the slowest-settling trial per sim/cdac-bit-settling/ and the analytically worst code per sim/mc-cdac-mismatch/), the free-MSB transition at 511->512 (where all nine switched weights change state but the deciding bit forms no ratio at all, because the free MSB is decided before any array switching -- a property DR-0014 keeps), weight-128 carries spanning the range, and both endpoints as the endpoint-fit anchors. Each transition is read at the trial that resolves it, from a full transistor-level conversion, against an ideal shadow DAC driven by the controller's own switch-driver outputs -- one conversion per transition, not a fine input search. NOT assumed binary-weighted-with-a-mid-scale-carry: see the netlist header.
- **Note**: NOMINAL vs STATISTICAL, stated so the two campaigns are not read as duplicating or as omitting each other's coverage: this record moves PVT with mismatch off (the harness default), sim/mc-cdac-mismatch/ and sim/comparator-offset-mc/ move mismatch with PVT held at nominal. spec/monte-carlo-methodology-memo.md Sec 4 states the same division from the Monte Carlo side, and sim/cdac-bit-settling/ Sec 5.3's finding that global process variation cancels in the charge-division ratio is why neither campaign needs to be run inside the other.
- **Note**: COMPARATOR OFFSET IS DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE THE ERROR NODE. A static input-referred offset is the ratified Offset row, measured by sim/comparator-offset-mc/, and consumes no INL/DNL budget. Only a CODE-DEPENDENT part would land here; spec/testbench-suite-memo.md carries that term explicitly.
- **Note**: V_cm is an ideal source: DR-0011's Consequences make V_cm generation an unbudgeted future deliverable, so there is no ratified envelope to model it against. Stated assumption, not a measured result.
- **Note**: The `cdac` corner set (7 process corners x 3 temperatures x 3 supplies = 63 points) is used rather than `mos`: this claim rides on the MiM sections, which a MOS-only sweep leaves at typical (sim/harness/README.md, 'Why the capacitor corners matter here').

- **Note**: Issue #123: this deck was regenerated onto the star-split in-path extraction that layout/toolchain.json's 875eac3 pin selects; the superseded record 20260806-052258-8d36824 measured the SAME manifest against the pre-bump lumped-stub extraction, whose 156 R sat on dead-end stubs carrying no signal current. Both records are retained -- the delta between them IS the in-path parasitic resistance's effect on static linearity. The deck also now carries a .save naming exactly the four vectors this manifest reads (see gen_extracted_core_tb.saved_vectors_lines): without it ngspice tries to store a transient waveform for all ~4256 new in-path leg nodes and every point dies before measuring. Retention only -- measurements are bit-identical with and without it (checked on tt_27c_3.30v).
